radiology_report:
Bravis Ziekenhuis | Radiology | 19 January 2025
Exam: multiparametric MRI of the prostate
Clinical indication: Evaluation of rising PSA (15.0 ng/mL) and prior positive biopsy findings. Clinical suspicion for clinically significant prostate cancer (PI-RADS 5).
FINDINGS:
The glandular volume registers at 42.78 mL. T2-weighted sequences highlight a focal hypointense focus within the right anterior mid-gland, spanning roughly 18 mm. High b-value DWI (b1000/b2000) shows pronounced restricted diffusion, mirrored by low ADC signal. DCE imaging captures early, focal, intense enhancement against the peripheral zone background. Neurovascular bundles remain bilateral and intact. No extraprostatic spread or seminal vesicle invasion is evident. Bladder and distal urethra appear normal.
IMPRESSION:
Focal lesion in the right anterior mid-gland exhibiting classic features of clinically significant prostate cancer.
PI-RADS 5.
Prostate volume 42.78 mL; PSA density 0.351 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.85514855.
